content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of lean beef, tofu and a variety of vegetables (e.g., bell pepper, zucchini, mushrooms). Carrots, broccoli, dark‑green leafy greens, potatoes and soy‑based sauces are excluded. This combination provides a balance of protein, vitamins and minerals without excess carbohydrates.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef is a rich source of iron, zinc and vitamin B12.
Tofu, made from soybeans, contains all essential amino acids.
The vegetables used are high in fiber and antioxidants that support digestive health.
Omitting potatoes lowers the dish’s glycemic index, making it more suitable for blood‑sugar control.
The recipe can be adapted to various cuisines by changing spices and cooking methods.

items.title: Supports muscle mass
items.content: Beef and tofu provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Boosts immunity
items.content: B‑vitamins and zinc from beef help maintain a healthy immune system.

items.title: Bone health
items.content: Tofu is often calcium‑fortified, and beef supplies phosphorus—both crucial for strong bones.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Fiber from the vegetables promotes intestinal motility and a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Reduces chronic disease risk
items.content: Antioxidants in the vegetables combat free radicals, lowering the risk of cardiovascular and cancerous diseases.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Beef can contain saturated fats; choose lean cuts and consume in moderation.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Tofu may trigger allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to soy.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Adding salt or pre‑made sauces can increase sodium; it’s best to control seasoning.

items.title: Protein digestion
items.content: Large protein portions may be heavy on the stomach for those with sensitive digestion.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sear lean beef pieces until browned, add cubed tofu and quickly stir‑fry. Then introduce the sliced vegetables, season with salt, pepper and your favorite herbs. Cook 5‑7 minutes until vegetables are tender, avoiding excess liquid.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Beef and tofu can be frozen separately in zip‑lock bags for up to 2 months.
